segments.t: Andrea rushes into the daycare center in absolute terror after finding her apartment empty. She discovers Jose Garcia happily cradling baby Flora, completely unbothered by her panic. Let's listen to their chaotic encounter in French first.

Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Flora! Oh, mon bébé adoré!
'Flora! Oh, my beloved baby!' Andrea bursts into tears of relief upon spotting her child. The possessive adjective 'my' introduces the masculine noun 'baby'.
Andréa, tout va très bien ici.
'Andrea, everything is going very well here.' Jose is startled by Andrea's frantic entrance. The phrase 'tout va bien' indicates that all is fine.
C'est un enlèvement d'enfant!
'It is a child abduction!' Andrea furiously accuses Jose of taking her daughter without consent. The compound noun 'enlevement d'enfant' means kidnapping.
Mais non, j'ai laissé un mot!
'Of course not, I left a note!' Jose defends himself by pointing to the note he wrote. The past tense 'have' comes from 'left'.
Tu es complètement fou, José!
'You are completely crazy, Jose!' Andrea vents her fury at his reckless behavior. The adjective 'crazy' describes someone out of their mind.
Regarde, elle est très heureuse.
'Look, she is very happy.' Jose points out that baby Flora is cooing and smiling peacefully. The feminine adjective 'happy' describes joy.
Bonjour Princesse Joues-rebondies!
'Hello Princess Chubby-cheeks!' Jose affectionately nicknames the baby after her round face. The compound term 'Chubby-cheeks' refers to plump cheeks.
Elle est où, la directrice?
'Where is the director?' Andrea demands to know who authorized Jose to bring Flora in. The question 'she' is colloquial for where is she.
Capucine s'occupe des autres enfants.
'Capucine takes care of the other children.' Jose explains that the daycare supervisor is in the next room. The verb phrase 's'occuper de' means to look after.
Allez, calme-toi et respire un peu.
'Come on, calm down and breathe a bit.' Jose coaches his stressed agent through breathing exercises. The imperative 'calm down' urges relaxation.
Regarde, nous sommes totalement zen.
'Look, we are totally zen.' Jose demonstrates how peaceful the nursery atmosphere is. The adjective 'calm' means relaxed and calm.
Une voiture t'attend pour le tournage.
'A car is waiting for you for the shoot.' Andrea reminds Jose of his strict filming schedule. The noun 'shoot' denotes a film shoot.
D'accord, je pars immédiatement.
'All right, I am leaving immediately.' Jose hands Flora over and prepares for his work day. The adverb 'immediately' indicates promptness.
Ne touche plus jamais à mon bébé!

'Never touch my baby again!' Andrea sets a firm boundary with her unpredictable star client. The negative structure 'ne ... plus jamais' means never again. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Andrea recovers her baby daughter safely from Jose Garcia at the daycare center. Relieved yet exhausted by the scare, she sends Jose off to his film set while hugging Flora tightly. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
À plus tard, maman stressée!
